observations.behavior: A completion recovery handler categorizes transport errors into HTTP responses with status/error-code fields, network errors, and other failures before reporting a recovery/error event.
observations.boundary: An error object format in source is not an observed service failure.

observations.behavior: Retry consideration combines network-kind failures, an initial resumed-stream state, or the active resume-request identity with an imported retryable-error predicate. Non-eligible failures are routed to ordinary or recoverable-error callbacks.
observations.boundary: The imported retry predicate was resolved in later saved-source review E2-098 (stream_resume_error_predicates). Classification still depends on token, identity, cancellation and retry guards and does not prove that a live retry occurred.

observations.behavior: On a permitted retry, the handler schedules a delayed resume attempt, reports recovery state, stores a cancellation callback that clears the timer and cancels a superseded request, and can pass resume token and offset into the new request.
observations.boundary: Actual timer firing, negotiated offsets and token validity were not observed.

observations.behavior: The recovery coordinator tracks attempted and successful resumes and emits attempted, succeeded, error, started and response event categories alongside current stream offset and attempt count.
observations.boundary: The presence of callbacks does not prove a successful resume occurred.

observations.behavior: The completion client can start from an existing stream topic or send a stream request; the handler also supports handoff from an initial request into a WebSocket topic and avoids duplicate completion delivery via close/failure guards.
observations.boundary: Neither actual WebSocket connection nor request-topic handoff was observed.

observations.behavior: A WebSocket topic path configures initial and idle timeout values, forwards decoded events through the recovery handler, and conditionally cancels the original request on socket completion or error.
observations.boundary: Source timeouts and fallback branches are not measurements of connectivity.

observations.behavior: The initial completion request has a separate request-level retry/refresh callback that rebuilds request integrity and identity headers when permitted. This is distinct from the resumption retry coordinator.
observations.boundary: The actual retry count and successful refreshed request cannot be inferred from the saved page.

observations.behavior: Before issuing the preparation request, the captured completion preparer checks cancellation and a supplied should-prepare guard. After an asynchronous device/identity lookup it repeats the cancellation and preparation guard. A rejected preparation guard exits without sending the request.
observations.boundary: These guards are source conditions. They do not show a cancelled or omitted live request.

observations.behavior: A preparation failure enters a distinct fallback only if the input contains a partial query, the caller permits retry, and an imported error eligibility predicate accepts the failure. After a randomized 250–500 ms delay, retry permission is checked again. One recursive preparation attempt changes dispatch to immediate, suppresses further retry, and revalidates should-prepare before sending.
observations.boundary: The imported preparation retry predicate was resolved in later saved-source review E2-097 (preparation_error_eligibility). The branch remains a source-level one-shot fallback with no observed retry or successful server response.

observations.behavior: A uniquely resolved captured module implements the preparation fallback eligibility predicate. It excludes abort/non-Error cases and selected terminal typed request error codes, honors a parsed structured can_retry=false veto, allows network errorKind or typed statuses 408/409/425/502/504, and applies timeout/offline/network-message heuristics to other Error objects.
observations.boundary: This predicate belongs to preparation fallback, not the separate stream-resumption retry coordinator. No live error or request retry is observed.

observations.behavior: The stream coordinator's uniquely shape-matched module exposes an automatic retry predicate (network kind or typed HTTP 408/409/425/429/502/504) and a different recoverable-error callback predicate (network kind or HTTP 4xx except 403 and selected terminal error codes). The two classifications have different purposes.
observations.boundary: Classification predicates remain gated by resume state and do not prove any actual request, retry or recovery callback occurred.

observations.behavior: The recovered helper consumes a resume-token control event into conversation/token state, advances offset and clears attempt count on acknowledged data, checks cancellation, identity, token and count guards, and computes bounded exponential backoff with a 0.5–1.0 random multiplier. Manual retry uses zero delay but retains core state guards.
observations.boundary: All state transitions and timings are captured code paths; stream events and timers have not been observed executing.

observations.behavior: The initial completion-stream caller enables automatic resume only when its history-and-training-disabled request field is not explicitly true. A separately invoked explicit-resume path supplies a true permission value. The shared coordinator still applies identity, abort, token/offset and retry-budget guards.
observations.boundary: The flag and distinct entrypoints are source-visible, but their live eligibility, invocation order and account-specific policies are unobserved.

fallback_scope: These values are fallback literals in the captured client and may be overridden by dynamic configuration, active request options, and different transport state. They are not contractual service guarantees. The preparation fallback's randomized 250–500 ms interval is a distinct source literal, not part of the configurable stream resume backoff budget.
open_questions: Check cancellation priority and delivery outcomes only with permitted synthetic runtime observations, if later desired.
Distinguish retry hints used only for display from those that actually schedule a client request.
Map callback delivery order and actual request cancellation outcomes only with authorized synthetic runtime evidence if later needed.
Other modality- or account-scoped resume gates beyond the reviewed history-and-training-disabled request flag require separate source tracing.
privacy: No original source code, endpoint strings, request headers, auth/account values, message content, URL, or extracted bundle filename is published.

preparation_fallback.limit: The guarded fallback uses a uniquely identified same-capture error eligibility module, now documented in preparation_error_eligibility. The method does not guarantee any retry occurs, nor does it establish a live network result.

resolved_import.boundary: The importer-to-predicate module relationship is source-backed; no runtime import or executed error branch is established.

decision_order.rule: Reject non-Error inputs and any Error whose name indicates an aborted request.
For a captured typed request error, reject model-cap, work-usage and conversation-not-found/deleted/expired terminal categories.
For a typed request error whose message parses into the expected structured shape, an explicit detail.can_retry=false rejects retry.
Otherwise, typed request errors are eligible only for a network errorKind or status in the captured allowlist.
For other Error instances, timeout name or browser offline state is enough for eligibility.
Other Error instances use fetch/network/DNS/connection message heuristics or a TypeError fallback that excludes several known non-retryable user/limits/auth/stale-conversation messages.

preparation_error_eligibility.scope: This is the error predicate used by completion preparation's partial-query fallback. The stream-resume recovery's separately imported retryability predicate is not attributed to this module.
preparation_error_eligibility.limit: The code's status field, errorKind and error class refer to captured client error objects. These source checks do not prove a server contract, what error was raised, or whether any retry was executed.

stream_resume_module_resolution.resolution_method: Cross-check all captured definitions sharing the short registry key against the three export slots and their call-site behavior; only one defines the required interface.
stream_resume_module_resolution.caveat: This establishes a captured static import relationship, not that the module was loaded or any retry ran in a browser.

automatic_retry.scope: The imported predicate supplies the automatic-retry eligibility flag to the resume coordinator; additional token/state/attempt guards still apply.

recoverable_callback.scope: This separate predicate decides whether an ineligible-for-retry failure can be routed to the recoverable-error callback instead of the ordinary error path.

stream_resume_error_predicates.contrast_to_preparation: The preparation predicate has a different typed HTTP allowlist without 429 and also inspects AbortError, terminal client errors and structured can_retry vetoes. Never apply one predicate's rules to the other.

resume_token_event.behavior: A recognized stream-token control event updates the stored conversation identity and resume token, notifies the token callback, and is not forwarded as an ordinary message update.

event_acknowledgement.behavior: A non-response-marker event acknowledgement increases the stored event offset by one; if retry attempts were pending, the success callback fires and the retry attempt counter resets to zero.

retry_gates: A resume-permission callback must be supplied.
An abort signal must not already be aborted.
A conversation identity must have been obtained.
A resume token is needed unless tokenless-resume is explicitly allowed.
Even when tokenless resume is allowed, a missing token is rejected after offset becomes positive.
Automatic retry additionally requires eligible error classification and an attempt count below the configured cap.
Manual retry bypasses automatic eligibility/cap but retains identity, token/offset and cancellation guards.

retry_backoff.scope: Values are captured defaults; the calling client may provide dynamic configuration overrides.

stream_resume_state_invariants.boundary: This is a captured state machine and a literal backoff formula, not observed timer execution, transport offsets, durable server recovery or a guarantee of successful resume.

initial_completion.gate: shouldAttemptResume is supplied as true unless the request's history_and_training_disabled field is explicitly true.

explicit_resume.gate: The separate explicit-resume handler construction supplies shouldAttemptResume=true.

resume_permission_wiring.downstream_guard: The imported resume coordinator checks the supplied resume-permission value before permitting an automatic retry, in addition to abort, token, identity and retry-budget conditions.
resume_permission_wiring.limits: This is a captured call-site boolean. It does not establish runtime account policy, that explicit resume is offered for the flagged request, or that a retry ever occurred.

source_reconciliation.method: Clarify historical limitations after additional source review without changing the initial stage descriptions or claiming runtime execution.
still_unverified: No actual preparation fallback or stream resume was observed executing.
No request outcome, server protocol guarantee or account-specific invocation policy was observed.
